thread:
ashwin: paging: High error-rate + 95th latency spike observed on inference-hosting in us-west-2. incident-bot auto-created PAGER (sev=2). Can folks join?
ops-bot: Incident PAGER: #2310004567 created. Trigger: api-edges > 7% 5xx and p95 latency > 1.2s for 3m. Pager routed to eng-oncall.
maya: I'm on it, jumping in. Initial ask: any customer-facing 5xx count?
ashwin: Yes — we saw a 5xx burst starting 12:02:14 UTC. Top affected route: /v1/complete (model: rwd-13b). 5xxs ~ 450 in 5m window, mostly 504s timeouts.
darya: I'm checking autoscaler/HPA metrics now, pulling k8s HPA status and GPU-pool telemetry.
kevin: Noted. If it's timeout-backed 504s, could be warmup delay causing requests to queue and hit gateway timeout.
ashwin: Timeline so far (quick): 12:01:50 burst of requests -> 12:02:10 HPA sees cpu% jump -> 12:02:30 queue depth spikes -> 12:03:00 requests start timing out -> 12:05:00 mitigation: reroute to fallback smaller model started.
maya: Share logs please — especially dproxy and autoscaler events.
darya: Pasting clipped logs (k8s HPA and pool):

```
$ kubectl get hpa rwd-runtime -n inference -o yaml
status:
  currentCPUUtilizationPercentage: 95
  currentReplicas: 6
  desiredReplicas: 12
  conditions:
    - type: ScalingActive
      status: "True"
    - type: AbleToScale
      status: "False"
      reason: InsufficientResourceQuotas
```

GPU pool telemetry (aggregated): GPU-util avg=78% -> 98% within 90s; AllocatedInstances=6 -> pendingProvision=4; warmup_inflight=3; avg_kv_cache_populate=420ms
```

kevin: HPA tried to scale, desiredReplicas=12 but AbleToScale=False — quota/cluster resource shortage. PendingProvision suggests cloud/GPU provisioning lag. Warmup_inflight and kv cache times show long initialization per new pod.
ashwin: Gateway logs show many requests hit a backend that returned 504 after 30s. Proxy had backlog ~240 reqs at peak.
maya: Customer impact: 4 enterprise tenants reported degraded responses, 2 with timeouts on user-facing flows. CS pinged us at 12:08.
sre-bot: added label: capacity-shortfall, warmup-delay, hpa-failure.
darya: Hypothesis A: HPA signaled correctly but cluster lacked quota/placement so scale-up was blocked -> backlog grew, warmup for newly provisioned nodes took ~20-40s to reach healthy -> requests hit gateway timeouts. Evidence: AbleToScale=False + pendingProvision.
darya: Hypothesis B: Continuous small-burst traffic pattern kept CPU metric noisy (spiky CPU) preventing early scale decisions; autoscaler minimum cooldown was too long, so scale-up reaction lagged. Evidence: CPU jitter logs and HPA scale event timestamps.
kevin: Also noticing model cold-start penalty: new pods spent time loading KV caches (avg_kv_cache_populate=420ms per shard) and restoring KV from s3. This added ~12-18s per pod before can serve full throughput.
ashwin: Running quick mitigation: 1) Reroute 20% of traffic to rwd-7b fallback (already triggered at 12:05), 2) manual node-provision request to cloud team (12:07), 3) reduce gateway timeout to 20s to free resources faster (12:09).
maya: Results: after reroute, p95 dropped to 800ms for remaining rwd-13b traffic, overall 5xx count reduced by ~60% by 12:12. Manual provisioner accepted request but actual instances started showing up at 12:18.
darya: Collected detailed metrics and attached condensed snippet:
- queue_depth (inference-queue): peak=240 at 12:03:10 -> back to <20 by 12:14
- hpa_scale_events: attempted at 12:02:45, 12:03:20 -> blocked due to quota
- gpu_pool_allocated: 6 -> desired 12 -> pending 4 -> provision start 12:07 -> ready 12:18
- warmup_success: new_pod_ready_to_serve avg=22s (includes KV load and kernels JIT)

kevin: Proposed in-thread mitigations and follow-ups:
- Short term: lower gateway timeout for long-model routes to 15s and enable immediate fallback to smaller model at 10s.
- Mid term: enforce a reserved buffer of idle GPUs for burst headroom (min_pool_reserved=2 for each region).
- Long term: add predictive pre-warm for models when traffic surge heuristics detected (e.g., sudden request-rate 2x in 30s).
- HPA tuning: consider multi-metric autoscaling with queue_depth as primary signal (not CPU only) and reduce stabilizationWindow for scale-up to 15s.

ashwin: Agreed. Also we should change the AbleToScale alert to fire earlier (when desiredReplicas > currentReplicas for > 30s). Right now it only fires after 5m.
maya: I'm drafting incident summary for CS and customers. Key points: root cause = capacity shortfall (quota + provisioning lag) + warmup delay on new replicas -> overload/backlog -> gateway timeouts. Mitigations taken: traffic reroute, manual provision, gateway timeout tuning.
darya: For RCA notebook I'll add timeline with logs, the HPA yaml snapshot, k8s events, and GPU provisioning traces. Will include reproduction steps and load profile used (saw many short requests with burstiness).
kevin: Quick dev note: QC of the model-serving image — JIT kernels take ~6-8s on first sequence; consider shipping pre-jit artifact or snapshot to reduce cold-start. Also examine KV cache parallelization to cut populate time.
ashwin: Action items (assign):
- darya: collect full event logs and produce timeline + attach to RCA doc (due EOD).
- kevin: prototype pre-jit snapshot plan and estimate impact on warmup (1 week).
- maya: customer comms draft and impact tally (due +2h).
- infra: (cc infra) evaluate quota/placement reason and propose reserved pool config (sync in 2h).
- sre: change AbleToScale alert threshold and add HPA blocked alarm (follow-up PR).

maya: any objections?
kevin: none from me. sounds good.
ashwin: closing pager for now — ops-bot, mark this as mitigated and continue RCA in-thread.
ops-bot: Incident PAGER #2310004567 status updated to mitigated by ashwin at 12:28 UTC.
maya: Adding final note: please include test harness that simulates 10k qps short-burst pattern for future load tests. That pattern triggered this hole.
darya: I'll upload link to the RCA doc when ready: https://internal.redwood/docs/rca/2310004567 (draft).
kevin: leaving +1. If infra needs extra ops credits to reserve GPUs, escalate to head of platform.
ashwin: thanks all, we'll reconvene tomorrow for postmortem and follow-ups.
